title: Dedicated capacity triage playbook: SLA-to-GPU-class mapping and scaling policy decision flow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a pragmatic, decision-oriented playbook for intake and prioritization of enterprise Dedicated capacity requests. The playbook must map requested SLA targets (p99 latency, sustained throughput, burst throughput) and commercial constraints (budget/commitment) to a recommended GPU class, reservation size, and autoscaling policy. It should include a concise scoring rubric to accelerate triage, guidance for limited-case fallbacks, operator runbook snippets for Dedicated onboarding, and a short set of template questions for sales/solutions engineers to collect during intake.
acceptance_criteria: Ship a one-page decision flow diagram + 2-page rubric document for PM/SE/Oncall use
Provide mapping table: SLA bands -> GPU class suggestions (A100/H100/Large-accelerator) and reservation sizing heuristics
Include a recommended default autoscaling policy per profile (steady, spiky, bursty) with guardrails and cost controls
Publish intake questionnaire template and scoring calculator for triage sessions
Stakeholder review completed: Solutions Eng, SRE, Sales Engineering, Legal (if regulatory)
notes: 2026-03-06: Kickoff with Solutions Eng and SRE to capture common failure modes and customer asks (latency-sensitive inference, large-batch offline reranking, embedding-heavy workloads).

2026-03-08: Collected 12 intake forms from recent enterprise deals; recurring themes: p99 150-300ms target, sustained throughput ranges 100-10k tokens/s, burst tolerance requests during daily batch windows.
2026-03-09: Early recommendation: map p99 <200ms to H100/low-latency profiles; p99 200-500ms to A100/quantized profiles; p99 >500ms to cost-optimized (T4/quantized) pools with best-effort SLO.
2026-03-10: Trade-off discussion: aggressive caching and KV prefix reuse can shift GPU class by 1 tier. Need to capture workload prompt shape and session vs stateless distribution in intake form.

2026-03-11: Review feedback from Security on regulatory workloads: require explicit KMS/HSM, audit log retention, and private control plane for high-privacy customers. Flag these for Private deployment conversation (not Dedicated).
decision_log: Decision 2026-03-09: Use a weighted score with dimensions: latency (0.35), sustained throughput (0.30), burst tolerance (0.15), cost sensitivity (0.10), regulatory/compliance (0.10).

Decision 2026-03-10: Autoscaling policy default set to: min_reserved = sustained_capacity; max_burst = 3x sustained for 30m windows; cooldown = 10m; pre-warm buffer recommended for predictable daily spikes.
Decision 2026-03-11: For p99 <200ms use H100-class or equivalent with dedicated single-tenant PCIe affinity and KV cache hot-sharding; require SLO SLA language for tail latency in contract.
scoring_rubric_summary: Compute a triage score: score = round(100*(0.35*latency_score + 0.30*throughput_score + 0.15*burst_score + 0.10*cost_score + 0.10*regulatory_score)). latency_score: 100 for p99<=150ms, 70 for 150-300ms, 40 for 300-500ms, 10 for >500ms. throughput_score: 100 for sustained>5000 tokens/s, 70 for 1000-5000, 40 for 200-1000, 10 for <200. burst_score: 100 if burst>5x, 70 if 3-5x, 40 if 1.5-3x, 10 if none. cost_score: 100 if high budget/commitment, 50 if medium, 10 if low. regulatory_score: 100 if requires additional compliance controls - route to Private, otherwise 0.
recommended_gpu_mapping: Sample mapping derived from scoring bands: 85-100 -> H100-class or multi-H100 reservation with KV hot-shard; 65-84 -> A100 80GB reservation w/ mixed-precision and optional quantized variants; 40-64 -> A100 40GB or T4 dense pools with aggressive quantization; <40 -> cost-optimized T4/CPU hybrid with best-effort SLO and caching suggestions.
autoscaling_templates: Steady (low variance): min_reserved = sustained_capacity; max = 1.25x sustained; scale_step = 1 GPU; cooldown = 15m; burst not expected.
Spiky (frequent short spikes): min_reserved = sustained_capacity * 0.8; max = sustained_capacity * 3; scale_step = 1-2 GPUs; cooldown = 5m; pre-warm windows supported.
Batch/bursty (predictable nightly): min_reserved = baseline; scheduled scaleup to peak 60m before window; max = peak; cooldown = 30m; use scheduled pre-allocation with burst credits.
fallback_strategies: Model variant fallback: automatically route to quantized / distilled model variant when Dedicated pool capacity constrained (with a contractually allowed accuracy delta).
Region fallback: failover to secondary region with compatible GPU family and explicit customer consent for cross-region data movement.
Degraded SLO mode: automatically reduce guarantee to best-effort with customer notification and billing credits as per negotiated bandwidth.
intake_questionnaire_template: Primary SLA targets: target p99 latency (ms), target p50 (ms), required availability/SLA %.
Workload profile: steady tokens/s, peak tokens/s, typical sequence length, session vs stateless distribution.
Accuracy tolerance: allowed model variant degradation (e.g., up to 5% metric drop) for cost or latency gains.
Budget & commitment: expected monthly committed spend and preferred billing model (commitment vs pay-as-you-go).
Compliance: data residency, encryption/KMS requirements, audit log retention, SSO/SCIM needs.
Expected ramp timeline and production date.
example_triage_case: Customer X requests p99 180ms, sustained 1500 tokens/s, bursts to 6000 tokens/s for 20m windows, medium budget, no extra compliance. Using rubric: latency_score=70, throughput_score=70, burst_score=100, cost_score=50, regulatory=0 -> overall ~73. Recommendation: A100 80GB reservation sized for sustained 1500 tokens/s with autoscale headroom to 2-3x for bursts; configure pre-warm for daily bursts and enable KV prefix caching to reduce headroom needs.
